source.title: Disparity Between Batches as a Signal for Early Stopping

record.tranche_reason: The study measures gradient disparity and reports how it relates to test error and generalization error across training settings; it also reports test-error trends as network width and batch size vary.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization capacity, magnitude-aware sharpness, or the optimizer and regularization comparisons in the versions. It reports several other gradient-disparity and generalization relationships, which are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates gradient disparity and early stopping. Its width sweep does not establish widening beyond the width needed for zero training error, as V2 requires. Its batch sweep stops at a training-loss threshold rather than a fixed epoch budget, as V5 requires. The other results measure constructs or interventions outside the supplied versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: gradient disparity is a promising early-stopping signal, especially with limited or noisy data, and tracks several generalization trends. Qualify its generality: cross-setting rankings fail at very large batch sizes, correlations vary, and Adam can show later divergence between gradient disparity and test loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates gradient disparity as a generalization metric and early-stopping criterion; it does not reproduce the methods in the listed original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relationships vary with batch size, training-set size, data augmentation, label-noise level, network width, and early-stopping threshold. At very large batch sizes, gradient disparity decreases after increasing over the smaller tested batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error decreases as ResNet, VGG and fully connected networks are widened on CIFAR-10, without establishing where these networks first fit the training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider networks can have lower image-classification test error across the tested width range.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient disparity correlates with test error across training-set sizes and label-noise conditions, and with generalization loss and error during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient disparity can track held-out performance and generalization gaps in some training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error increases with batch size in the reported loss-threshold experiments; gradient disparity eventually decreases at very large batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size can affect test error even when training ends at a common loss threshold, while gradient disparity need not rank performance across very large batches.

record.problems: The batch-size and width trend values are shown in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The batch-size sweep stops at a training-loss threshold, not a fixed epoch budget. The authors note that gradient-based similarity metrics are not informative when gradients are very small.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Other reported comparisons concern early-stopping performance against cross-validation or alternative metrics, rather than the claim versions' behaviors.

untested.parts: The required conjunction of random-label memorization capacity and natural-label generalization is not established by the recorded correlations or readable numerical results.
Continued test-error improvement beyond the width needed for zero training error; convergence without explicit regularization and the specified one-hidden-layer setting.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization under comparable training, the contribution of locality, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions and recovery interventions.
Large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their removal through recipe adaptations.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout, including dataset-size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gap and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V2 supports label: an overall width trend does not establish improvement past the fitting threshold. States of cannot_determine refer to the supplied claim versions, not to the validity of the reported correlations. The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values establishing additional qualifying effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
The paper reports width-related test-error trends, but does not establish zero training error, the interpolation threshold, or the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU setup.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks' test error or local-connectivity effect.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out performance comparison.
Batch size is varied, but the reported sweep stops at a training-loss threshold rather than holding epoch budgets fixed; it does not test the stated recipe adaptations.
The study measures gradient disparity, not magnitude-aware sharpness or perturbation tolerance.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: CNN and fully connected neural networks
rows.size_stated: different number of channels and hidden units; scale=1 recovers original configurations
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; training endpoint not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied network width and measured test error and normalized gradient disparity.

conditions.value: convolutional neural networks and fully connected neural networks

rows.value: The text states test error decreases with network width; individual values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper states that test error decreases with width for ResNet, VGG, and fully connected networks; this does not establish behavior past an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: The reported decrease in test error with width is valid, but neither Section 6 nor Figures 8 and 20 establish zero training error or locate the width needed to fit. This cannot establish V2's post-fit width effect. The row also combines ResNet, VGG and fully connected networks rather than recording their results separately.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with different training set sizes
rows.operation_detail: Measured the relationship between gradient disparity and test error across training-set sizes.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between gradient disparity and test error
rows.note: Correlation reported for the data-augmentation setting.
rows.check: The correlation 0.979 is correctly reported. Gradient disparity versus test error does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gap, or another supplied version.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with different training set sizes
rows.operation_detail: Measured the relationship between gradient disparity and test error across training-set sizes.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between gradient disparity and test error
rows.check: The correlation 0.984 is correctly reported, but measures gradient disparity versus test error rather than any supplied version.

rows.subject: networks trained on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
rows.stage_stated: trained until training loss is below 0.01
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size and measured test error and gradient disparity.
rows.measure: Test error and gradient disparity across batch sizes
rows.value: The text states that both increase with batch size for not-too-large batches; at very large batches, gradient disparity decreases. Individual values are figure only.
rows.note: The text says gradient disparity matches test-error rankings only when batch sizes are not too large; training stopped at a loss threshold, not a fixed epoch budget.
rows.check: Figures 7 and 23 stop training below loss 0.01, so they cannot establish V5's fixed-epoch penalty. The downturn at very large batches concerns gradient disparity; it does not establish a partial or reversed test-error penalty. Separate datasets, architectures and measures into individual rows.

rows.subject: 4-layer fully connected neural network with 500 hidden units
rows.stage_stated: trained on the entire MNIST dataset with 0% label noise
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlations between gradient disparity and generalization loss and error over training iterations.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation with generalization loss and generalization error
rows.note: The authors say the generalization error is the difference between test and training errors.
rows.check: Both correlations are correctly reported, but gradient disparity is not magnitude-aware sharpness. These results cannot establish any supplied version.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.stage_stated: trained on a subset of 12.8 k points of the MNIST training dataset
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlations between gradient disparity and test error and test loss over training iterations and label-noise levels.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between gradient disparity and test error/test loss
rows.note: The figure caption reports correlations over all iterations and label-noise levels.
rows.check: Both correlations are correctly reported. Pooling correlations over iterations and label-noise levels does not establish V1's conjunction of near-perfect random-label fitting, chance random-label test accuracy and strong natural-label generalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
